en.headline: Three Hong Kong newspapers raise cover prices by HK$3 this month
en.dek: Ming Pao rose to HK$15 from Sunday, while the Hong Kong Economic Times and Hong Kong Economic Journal will follow on Monday.
body: Three Chinese-language newspapers in Hong Kong have raised their retail prices by HK$3 this month, the first sector-wide adjustment in two years.

Ming Pao increased its single-copy price from HK$12 to HK$15 on Sunday, a rise of 25 per cent. The Hong Kong Economic Times will move from HK$12 to HK$15 on Monday, while the Hong Kong Economic Journal will rise from HK$15 to HK$18, an increase of 20 per cent.

The previous round of Chinese-newspaper price rises occurred in November 2024, when several titles moved from HK$10 to HK$12 and the Journal went from HK$12 to HK$15. News vendors have previously said similar increases can reduce overall sales.
Readers who buy the titles regularly will see the higher prices at newsstands from the respective start dates.

zh.headline: 三份本地報章本月加價3元 明報今起調至15元
zh.dek: 明報由周日每份12元加至15元，經濟日報及信報則由周一起分別加至15元及18元。
body: 本港三份中文報章本月起加價3元，是兩年來首次同業調整售價。
明報由周日每份12元上調至15元，加幅25%。香港經濟日報由周一起由12元加至15元，信報則由15元加至18元，加幅20%。
上一次中文報章加價是在2024年11月，當時多份報章由10元加至12元，信報則由12元加至15元。報販以往曾表示加價後整體銷量可能下跌。
讀者由相關生效日起在報攤購買這些報章時將支付新售價。
